{"slug": "website-builder-for-restaurants", "title": "AI Website Builder for Restaurants: Launch in Minutes", "metaTitle": "AI Website Builder for Restaurants: Launch in Minutes", "metaDescription": "Describe your restaurant in chat and Kodely builds a real website - menu, hours, location, photos, and a reserve-a-table form. Free to start, live in minutes.", "targetKeyword": "website builder for restaurants", "category": "Industries", "bodyHtml": "

What Restaurant Websites Actually Need

A restaurant site has a narrower job than most business websites, but it has to nail every part of that job. A hungry visitor lands on the page and wants five things fast: what you serve, when you're open, where you are, what the place feels like, and how to get a table. Miss any one of those and they close the tab and pick the next search result. A restaurant website builder that skips straight to generic templates misses this - a restaurant page succeeds or fails on specifics, not polish.

That's the gap Kodely is built for. You describe your restaurant in plain English in a chat interface, and Kodely writes a real website around those five needs - not a form-filled template, an actual coded app you can keep shaping.

The Must-Have Sections

  • Menu - organized by category (starters, mains, drinks) with prices, easy to scan on a phone
  • Hours and location - clear open/close times per day and an address block visitors can find in seconds
  • Atmosphere - a visual layout built to showcase food and interior photography once you drop your own images in
  • Story - a short about section covering who you are and why the food is worth the trip
  • Reserve a table - a contact-style form for name, party size, date, and phone number
  • Contact and social - phone number, email, and links to your social profiles

A Real Example Prompt

Here's the kind of prompt that gets you a working restaurant site on the first try:

Prompt: Build a website for Mesa Verde, a modern Mexican restaurant in Austin. Homepage with a bold hero section and our tagline 'Tacos worth the drive.' A menu page with three sections - tacos, entrees, and drinks - each item with a name, short description, and price. An about page telling our story of family recipes passed down three generations. A location page with our address, hours (Tuesday to Sunday, 5pm to 11pm, closed Monday), and a map-style block. A Reserve a Table page with a form for name, phone, party size, and preferred date. Warm color palette - deep red and cream - with a modern serif font for headings.

Kodely turns that into a multi-page app with working navigation, real layout components, and copy that matches what you described - ready to refine from there.

What Kodely Generates

This is the part that separates Kodely from drag-and-drop builders: what comes out is a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application, built from a foundation codebase with hand-built UI primitives - not raw HTML and not a static mockup. Every page is made of real component files you could hand to a developer. The live preview you watch update as you chat is the actual compiled app rendering, not a screenshot.

Two honest limits worth knowing up front. First, the photos and atmosphere sections start as styled placeholder visuals - Kodely generates the layout and composition for showcasing food and interior shots, but you supply the real photography yourself, it isn't pulled in automatically. Second, the Reserve a Table page is a contact-form UI, not a live booking system - it doesn't process real reservations, send confirmation emails, or take payments. If you need an actual appointment or booking workflow, read our guide on building a booking and appointment website with AI. For most restaurants, a strong informational site with a reservation-request form covers the job - visitors submit their info and you call or text to confirm.

Customizing In Chat

Once the first version is up, refine it the same way you built it: describe the change in chat. 'Make the menu two columns on desktop,' 'add a catering section,' 'swap the hero image for something darker' - Kodely edits the real components behind the scenes. Every successful generation saves a checkpoint, so if a change goes sideways, rolling back to the previous version is free and instant. You can also open code view at any point to see and copy the actual source files Kodely generated.

Publishing It Live

When the site looks right, one click publishes it to a live public URL at yourrestaurant.kodely.site - included at no extra cost, no separate hosting step to configure. Every publish is automatically scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live, so you're not shipping something you'll regret. Custom domains and code export aren't available yet - today it's the kodely.site subdomain and in-app code viewing.

Credits and Getting Started

Kodely gives every new account 750 free credits, no credit card required, which is enough to build and iterate on a full restaurant site. Credits are metered from real AI cost, and if a generation fails to compile, you're never charged for it. Need more room to experiment? Top-ups start at $9 for 500 credits, and credits never expire - see full details on pricing.

FAQ

Does Kodely handle real restaurant reservations or online orders?

Not yet. The Reserve a Table section Kodely builds is a contact-form UI - visitors submit their request, but there's no backend processing reservations, payments, or online ordering behind it. For most restaurants this works fine as a lead-capture form you follow up on directly.

Can I use my own domain, like mesaverde.com?

Not currently. Published sites live on a free *.kodely.site subdomain. Custom domain support isn't available yet.

Can I download the website's code?

You can view and copy the generated source files from code view inside Kodely. There's no zip export or download option yet.

Do I need design or coding experience?

No. You describe the restaurant and what you want in plain English, and Kodely writes the actual React components. Editing later works the same way - just describe the change.

What if I want click-to-edit instead of chat?

Kodely is chat-based editing only right now - there's no visual click-to-edit canvas yet. Every change goes through a chat message, which also means every change is tracked as a checkpoint you can roll back to.

Build your restaurant site free - 750 credits, no credit card required, live on a real URL today.
